name: Contemplative Landscape Model Scores of Downtown Singapore Walks (SP-Scheme)
description:
Method replication: same task, scales and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (84 new Google Street View views of the same four downtown Singapore walking routes). Experts score street views on the 7 components of the Contemplative Landscape Model (CLM): layers of the landscape, landform, vegetation, color and light, compatibility, archetypal elements, and character of peace and silence, each from 1 to 6 with the paper's scoring guide (anchors for 1–2, 3–4 and 5–6) under every scale. The contemplative landscape (CL) score of a view is the mean of the 7 components; the paper compares views and routes (Esplanade Park, Museum Area, Robinson Road, Raffles Place Park) and maps the scores. Views are 120° wide and 55° high (25° above and 30° below the horizon), as in the paper: view 1 looks along the route, view 2 the opposite way, view 3 to the side.

Original study: Hou, Masoudi, Chadala & Olszewska-Guizzo (2020), Remote Sensing 12(21), 3517. 68 points about 20 m apart on 4 routes, 3 views per point (204 views) from 360° photos (RICOH Theta Z1, January 2020); 3 trained landscape-architecture experts scored every view (inter-rater kappa 0.71).

Differences from the original study: (1) the views are Google Street View panoramas (car or trekker, 2010–2026) instead of the authors' own 360° photos taken on foot in January 2020, so a few viewpoints sit on the road rather than on the footpath; (2) 28 points (6, 8, 7 and 7 per route) spaced evenly along routes traced from the paper's map, instead of 68 points every 20 m; (3) view 3 is chosen automatically as the side with more sky and greenery, instead of by the authors avoiding a facade; (4) each participant scores one randomly assigned route (18–24 views) in random order, instead of 3 experts scoring all views; (5) added consent, a scoring-guide page with a one-line explanation of archetypal elements, and four background questions (profession, years of experience, prior CLM use, familiarity with downtown Singapore). Images: © Google Street View.
author: Hou, Y., Masoudi, M., Chadala, A., & Olszewska-Guizzo, A.

elements.name: consent
elements.title: I agree to take part. My answers are recorded anonymously for research.

elements.name: route
elements.title: The walking route assigned to this participant and the order its views were shown (route name, list of view files)

elements.name: layers
elements.title: Layers of the landscape
elements.description: 1–2: Layers do not enhance the overall visual quality, or there are no layers. 3–4: Layers moderately enhance the overall visual quality. 5–6: Far-distance view (400 m or more); layers greatly enhance the visual quality.

elements.name: landform
elements.title: Landform
elements.description: 1–2: Flat or rugged landform. 3–4: Landform is not very significant to the setting, or hard to say. 5–6: Undulating landform, natural lines.

elements.name: vegetation
elements.title: Vegetation
elements.description: 1–2: Low diversity of vegetation, few native species; no seasonal changes. 3–4: Moderate diversity of vegetation, moderate changes across the seasons. 5–6: High diversity of species, plants seem native; seasonally changing vegetation.

elements.name: color_light
elements.title: Color and light
elements.description: 1–2: Lots of vivid, contrasting colors; light and shade are not visible. 3–4: Moderate amount of contrasting colors, moderate amount of light and shade. 5–6: Natural, broken or warm colors, and visible light and shade.

elements.name: compatibility
elements.title: Compatibility
elements.description: 1–2: Physical and visual relations are not worked out, or chaos / lack of harmony. 3–4: Physical and visual relations are not clear, or some elements disturb the harmony and balance. 5–6: Physical and visual relations are worked out: explicit spatial order, harmony, balance between natural and created.

elements.name: archetypal
elements.title: Archetypal elements
elements.description: 1–2: No archetypal elements. 3–4: Archetypal elements are present but not important for the overall perception. 5–6: Archetypal elements strongly influence the overall perception.

elements.name: peace
elements.title: Character of peace and silence
elements.description: 1–2: No character of peace and silence: busy, no contrast with the urban environment. 3–4: Moderate, and/or a moderate sense of solitude, and/or less contrast with the urban environment. 5–6: Explicit, in contrast to the urban environment; invites to rest and relax and gives a sense of solitude.
